title: The Early Church — Acts of the Apostles
description: Test your knowledge of the early church and the Book of Acts!

questions.question: What happened on the Day of Pentecost?
options: The Holy Spirit came upon the believers
questions.explanation: On the Day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit came upon the believers with the sound of wind and what looked like tongues of fire (Acts 2:1-4).

questions.question: How many people believed and were baptized after Peter's sermon at Pentecost?
questions.explanation: About 3,000 people believed in Jesus and were baptized after Peter preached at Pentecost (Acts 2:41).

questions.question: What four things did the early believers devote themselves to?
options: Teaching, fellowship, breaking bread, and prayer
questions.explanation: Acts 2:42 says the early believers devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayer.

questions.question: Who was the first person to die for his faith in Jesus?
questions.explanation: Stephen was the first Christian martyr. He was stoned to death for his bold witness about Jesus (Acts 7:54-60).

questions.question: What were Stephen's last words?
options: 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them'
questions.explanation: Like Jesus on the cross, Stephen forgave his killers, saying, 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them' (Acts 7:60).

questions.question: What happened to Saul on the road to Damascus?
options: A bright light from heaven blinded him and Jesus spoke to him
He decided to become a fisherman
questions.explanation: A brilliant light from heaven flashed around Saul, and he heard Jesus say, 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?' (Acts 9:3-4).

questions.question: How many missionary journeys did Paul make?
questions.explanation: Paul made three great missionary journeys across the Roman Empire, starting new churches in many cities.

questions.question: What did Paul write to the churches he started?
options: Letters that became books of the New Testament
questions.explanation: Paul wrote letters (epistles) to encourage and teach the churches. Many became New Testament books like Romans, Corinthians, and Ephesians.
